Package com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.client.picker

Class PickerExporter

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.client.picker.PickerExporter
public final class PickerExporter extends Object
Turns picker drafts into datapack JSON. Every config field is a required codec field, so ConfigFile.CODEC's own encode already produces the canonical, every-field-explicit form the shipped data uses. Two entry points:
  • export() — the single committed mob, sent to the server as a PickerExportPacket; the creative-gated server handler validates it, writes world/datapacks/somegoogly-picker/data/<ns>/eyes/<entity>.json, and /reloads so it persists and re-syncs through the normal path. Works from a remote client; the result arrives as a server chat message (rate-limited server-side to one export per 10 seconds).
  • exportAll() — a purely client-side dump of every eye config into <gameDir>/somegoogly-export/data/…: the synced runtime state (ClientEyeConfigs) for untouched entities, overlaid with the picker's per-entity drafts (PickerState.authoredConfigs()) so a mob saved-but-never-exported is included too. For copying straight into the mod's resources/.

  • Method Details

    • export

      public static net.minecraft.network.chat.Component export()
      Send the committed draft for the chosen mob to the server to be written and reloaded. Client-side we only guard the obvious (something committed) and codec-encode the draft; all real validation — and the authoritative feedback — is the server's (PickerExportService).

    • exportAll

      public static net.minecraft.network.chat.Component exportAll()
      Dump every eye config to one canonical file per entity under <gameDir>/somegoogly-export/data/<ns>/eyes/<entity>.json: the synced runtime state for untouched entities, with each picker draft overlaid on its entity (so saved-but-not-exported mobs are written too). Unlike the per-mob export this is entirely client-side (no server involvement, no reload) — it just captures what's authored/live so it can be copied into the mod's resources/.

      The declared version range is re-synthesized from the currently-loaded version of each entity's namespace (VersionRangeMatcher.rangeFor(java.lang.String)); the original entry's declared range isn't preserved in the runtime config, so it can't be recovered.
